TEARDOWN terminates the session; Session header is no longer valid after TEARDOWN

ALL.CSeq: Mandatory in every request and every response. Must be a monotonically increasing integer per method.
ALL (AFTER SETUP).Session: Required in all requests after SETUP has been successfully completed. Server assigns Session ID in SETUP response.
SETUP.Transport: Required in SETUP request. Specifies transport parameters (RTP/UDP, RTP/TCP, unicast/multicast, client/server ports).
OPTIONS.Public: Response header listing all supported methods. Present in 200 OK response to OPTIONS.
DESCRIBE.Accept: Typically set to application/sdp in the request. Response Content-Type should be application/sdp.
DESCRIBE.Content-Type: Response header set to application/sdp when SDP body is present.
PLAY.Range: Optional. Specifies NPT (Normal Play Time) or clock range. Format: npt=start-end or clock=YYYYMMDDTHHMMSSZ-
PAUSE.Range: Optional. Specifies pause point. If omitted, pause occurs immediately.
REDIRECT.Location: Required in REDIRECT request. Specifies the new URL for the client to connect to.
ANNOUNCE.Content-Type: Required. Must be application/sdp when posting session description.
SET_PARAMETER.Content-Type: Required. Type of parameter representation (e.g., text/parameters).
SET_PARAMETER.Content-Length: Required. Length of parameter body.
GET_PARAMETER.Content-Type: Optional. If body present, specifies type of parameter representation.
ALL.Content-Length: Required if message body is present. Specifies byte length of body.
ALL.User-Agent: Optional. Client identification string.

status_changes.description: INIT -> INIT via OPTIONS
status_changes.rationale: Heuristic trace augmentation directly shows this transition. Consistent with RFC 2326 where OPTIONS can be sent at any time without changing state.

status_changes.description: INIT -> DESCRIBED via DESCRIBE
status_changes.rationale: Heuristic trace augmentation directly shows this transition. Consistent with standard RTSP lifecycle where DESCRIBE is the first method after OPTIONS.

status_changes.description: DESCRIBED -> READY via SETUP
status_changes.rationale: Heuristic trace augmentation directly shows this transition. SETUP establishes transport and transitions to READY state per RFC 2326.

status_changes.description: INIT -> READY via SETUP
status_changes.rationale: Heuristic trace augmentation shows this transition, but it bypasses DESCRIBE. While possible per RFC, it's less common and the evidence is only from heuristic augmentation.

status_changes.description: READY -> PLAYING via PLAY
status_changes.rationale: Heuristic trace augmentation directly shows this transition. This is the canonical transition per RFC 2326.

status_changes.description: PAUSED -> PLAYING via PLAY
status_changes.rationale: Heuristic trace augmentation shows this transition, but the invariant claim says PLAY transitions from READY to PLAYING and PAUSE transitions from PLAYING to READY, not PAUSED. There's a discrepancy between the transition claim and the invariant claim about PAUSED state.

status_changes.description: PLAYING -> PAUSED via PAUSE
status_changes.rationale: Heuristic trace augmentation shows this transition, but the invariant claim states PAUSE transitions from PLAYING to READY, not PLAYING to PAUSED. There is a state naming inconsistency.

status_changes.description: PLAYING -> CLOSED via TEARDOWN
status_changes.rationale: Heuristic trace augmentation directly shows this transition. Consistent with RFC 2326 where TEARDOWN terminates the session.

status_changes.description: READY -> CLOSED via TEARDOWN
status_changes.rationale: Heuristic trace augmentation directly shows this transition. Consistent with RFC 2326 where TEARDOWN is valid from READY state.

status_changes.description: RECORDING -> CLOSED via TEARDOWN
status_changes.rationale: Heuristic trace augmentation directly shows this transition. Consistent with RFC 2326 where TEARDOWN is valid from RECORDING state.

status_changes.description: CSeq header is mandatory in every request and every response, monotonically increasing per method
status_changes.rationale: Well-established RFC 2326 requirement. The LLM Spec Agent confirms this and it is a fundamental RTSP protocol invariant.

status_changes.description: SETUP must precede PLAY, PAUSE, and RECORD
status_changes.rationale: Standard RTSP protocol requirement per RFC 2326. SETUP establishes the session and transport before playback or recording can begin.

status_changes.description: Session header is required in all requests after SETUP has been completed
status_changes.rationale: Standard RTSP protocol requirement. The server assigns a Session ID in the SETUP response, and subsequent requests must include it.

status_changes.description: DESCRIBE typically precedes SETUP but is not strictly required
status_changes.rationale: Per RFC 2326, DESCRIBE is recommended but not mandatory before SETUP. The LLM Spec Agent confirms this.

status_changes.description: OPTIONS can be sent at any time, in any state
status_changes.rationale: Per RFC 2326, OPTIONS is a stateless method that can be sent at any time. The transition claim INIT->INIT via OPTIONS also supports this.

status_changes.description: TEARDOWN terminates the session; Session header is no longer valid after TEARDOWN
status_changes.rationale: Standard RTSP protocol behavior per RFC 2326. TEARDOWN explicitly terminates the session.

status_changes.description: Transport header is required in SETUP request
status_changes.rationale: Per RFC 2326, the Transport header is mandatory in SETUP requests to specify transport parameters.

status_changes.description: Canonical lifecycle: OPTIONS -> DESCRIBE -> SETUP -> PLAY -> TEARDOWN
status_changes.rationale: This is the standard RTSP lifecycle per RFC 2326. The transition claims support this sequence.

status_changes.description: PAUSE transitions from PLAYING to READY; PLAY from READY to PLAYING
status_changes.rationale: The transition claims show PLAYING -> PAUSED via PAUSE and PAUSED -> PLAYING via PLAY, which contradicts this invariant's state naming (PAUSED vs READY). There is inconsistency between the claims.

status_changes.description: RECORD is valid only from READY state, transitions to RECORDING
status_changes.rationale: The LLM Spec Agent supports this, but there is no direct trace evidence provided for this transition in the claims.

status_changes.description: TEARDOWN is valid from READY, PLAYING, or RECORDING states; transitions to INIT
status_changes.rationale: The transition claims show TEARDOWN transitions to CLOSED, not INIT. There is a state naming discrepancy between the invariant (INIT) and the transition claims (CLOSED).

status_changes.description: GET_PARAMETER and SET_PARAMETER can be sent at any time, with or without an active session
status_changes.rationale: The LLM Spec Agent supports this, but no direct trace evidence is provided for these methods in the claims.

status_changes.description: DESCRIBE may return 404 if resource not found; client may retry with different URL
status_changes.rationale: The LLM Spec Agent references Session 3 and Session 6, but no trace evidence is provided in the claims to verify this.

status_changes.description: Default RTSP port is 554; alternative port is 8554
status_changes.rationale: Well-known standard per RFC 2326 and IANA assignments. This is a factual protocol specification detail.

status_changes.description: Media data travels over RTP/RTCP on separate channels, not over RTSP itself
status_changes.rationale: Fundamental RTSP protocol design per RFC 2326. RTSP is a control protocol; media uses RTP/RTCP.
